newsitem.title: ANTIGUA AND BARBUDA: Caricom summit ends ahead of series of trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Caricom summit ends ahead of series of trade talks.

text.p: Heads of government of the 14-member Caribbean Community (Caricom) on Friday ended a two-day summit, saying they had prepared for a series of crucial trade talks during the coming year.
At the meeting, Shridath Ramphal, a former Guyanese secretary-general, was named the region's new trade commissioner.

Ramphal will be responsible for negotiating a series of free trade accords with countries in the Western Hemisphere. He will also lead talks on Caricom's entry into the Free Trade Agreement of the Americas and discussions with the European Union on a Lome trade-and-aid accord to replace the current pact, which expires in three years.

Haitian President Rene Preval and Leonel Fernandez, president of the Dominican Republic, attended the summit although their nations are not Caricom members. They agreed to use the joint negotiating mechanisms of which Ramphal was put in charge, particularly in regard to the Lome negotiations.

The heads of government met on Friday with Uruguayan Foreign Minister Alvaro Ramos, who represented the Mercosur trade bloc, whose full members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. He signalled the group's desire to enter a free trade agreement with Caricom, which represents the English-speaking countries of Caribbean.
Ramos said those discussions likely would begin next week in Recife, Brazil, when trade ministers begin the next round of talks on the Free Trade Agreement of the Americas.

Noting that Chile and Bolivia have signed trade accords with the four Mercosur members and the Andean Pact countries were likely to do so shortly, Caricom officials said they also would like to have preferred market access.
Discussions have also begun on a free trade accord between Caricom and the Dominican Republic, and further action was expected in July when Fernandez attends the next Caricom summit in Jamaica.

At that session, Caricom officials said the group would begin to consider negotiating a free trade with Cuba, Caricom officials said. Trinidad and Tobago has decided to negotiate its own agreement with Cuba, leaving the door open for the rest of the region to do so later.
"We have not gone into the details," said Trinidad Foreign Minister Ralph Maraj, referring to the talks with Cuba. "But something has to happen this year with respect to that."
The region had hoped to sign at least three trade accords in 1997, but this is now looking less and less likely.
"We have lost a bit of time," said Jamaican Prime Minister P.J. Patterson. "I'm not sure we can get three this year, but we should have them in place within 12 months from now."
